display.purpose: The single hero figure per screen (e.g. total across accounts). Used once, sparingly.

headline.purpose: Page titles and the primary value in a section.

body.purpose: The workhorse — nearly all UI text, cells, descriptions.

label.purpose: Hints, metadata, badges, and uppercase section eyebrows.

shadows.name: floating-overlay
shadows.purpose: The 'More' popover / menus — lifted above the page, will dismiss.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: Mobile navigation drawer, above the scrim.

shadows.name: scroll-edge
shadows.purpose: Header once content scrolls beneath it (appears past 4px scroll).

shadows.name: segment-thumb
shadows.purpose: Selected theme-toggle segment, proud of its recessed track.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Confident arrivals — progress grow, chat rise, reasoning unfold.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Active-state dip applied to every button and .press element.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: The authored moment — a recommendation's reasoning animating its own height open via interpolate-size.

motion.name: theme-flip
motion.purpose: Eased light-dark switch on the body.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action — solid Signal Orange, physical press feedback, no hover colour shift.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral action — hairline border, fills to surface-2 on hover.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Low-stakes action — muted text, no border, lifts to full ink on hover.

components.name: Solid Button (neutral)
components.description: High-emphasis action in a neutral key — solid ink fill, canvas text. Used where a form's main action would put a second Signal Orange on screen (transactions Filter, import confirm); carries a primary's weight without breaking the One Voice Rule.

components.name: Input Field
components.description: A well cut into the card — canvas-coloured background, border shifts to Signal Orange on focus (no ring).

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat bordered surface with an uppercase eyebrow over a large tabular hero figure.

components.name: Status Badges
components.description: Fully-round pills; default is a quiet surface-2, semantic tones use a 12% tint of their colour.
components.html: move cash on track behind loss

components.name: Nav Links
components.description: Rounded text links; the active item fills to surface-2 with medium-weight ink.

components.name: Progress Bar
components.description: Recessed pill track; the fill grows from its left edge to its value on mount, so it reads as 'how far'.

components.name: Recommendation Card
components.description: The signature component — a suggestion with a benefit chip and a 'Why this?' disclosure that unfolds its reasoning trace inside a left-border margin rule. Embodies the 'no black box' POV.

components.name: Loading Skeleton
components.description: Route-level loading fallback — pulsing surface-2 blocks that echo the page's own chrome (header, hero card, detail rows), shown while the next segment streams in. Freezes to a static shape under reduced-motion; announced as a role=status region.

components.name: Route Fallback (error / not-found)
components.description: Centred surface card for the error and not-found routes, rendered inside the app shell. Error uses the warn (caution) register with a Try again retry() and hides the raw message; not-found is neutral. Copy reassures nothing was changed and offers the way back.

components.name: Defined Term (Explainer)
components.description: A jargon term set with a dotted underline that reveals a one-sentence plain-language gloss on hover, keyboard focus, or tap. role=tooltip + aria-describedby carry it to screen readers, the global focus ring shows on keyboard focus, and Esc dismisses without moving focus (WCAG 1.4.13). Definitions come from one shared glossary so a term reads identically everywhere; in forms the same meaning is persistent helper text instead.
components.html: How many months your instantly-available cash would cover essential spending if your income stopped.

components.name: Command Palette (⌘K)
components.description: A keyboard-first overlay reaching every page and core action across a 12-page app. ⌘K / Ctrl-K (or the header Search chip) opens a centred surface panel — the sanctioned floating pattern (border, shadow-xl, pop-in) over the drawer scrim. Combobox + listbox: the field keeps focus and drives an aria-activedescendant cursor so ↑/↓ move, ↵ runs, and Esc closes and returns focus to where it was. One Voice holds — the only accent is the focus ring; the active row is a neutral surface-2 fill, never orange. The 12 routes are shared with the nav so the two can't drift; the trigger chip shows at lg and up.

components.name: Bulk Actions Bar (multi-select)
components.description: The transactions ledger doubles as a triage surface: a checkbox column and a "select page" checkbox drive a bar that replaces the toolbar hint the moment rows are ticked — "N selected", then recategorise, make a rule, export CSV, delete. When the whole page is ticked and more match, a banner offers "Select all N matching this filter", applied server-side by that same filter (not a list of ids). One Voice holds: ticked rows take a neutral surface-2 tint (never orange), the verbs are bordered neutral controls, and only Delete borrows the neg register — through the same two-step ConfirmButton + Undo toast the single-row delete uses. Delete removes only user-entered rows and reports what it kept; recategorise skips transfers; make-a-rule writes KEYWORD auto-categorise rules for future imports and files the current rows too.

narrative.overview:
Finance OS is a warm glass cockpit for a person's money: instrument-grade clarity delivered in the voice of a well-set financial column. Every figure is legible at a glance, every figure traces back to source, and the interface is forever answering the same four questions — what do I have, what's happening this month, what should I do, am I on track — without ever hiding the arithmetic behind a black-box score. The chrome recedes; the numbers lead.

The palette is 'sunset and ink' — a pale-sunlight canvas (or deep-navy at night) with deep-navy ink, warmed by a family of golds and oranges that each mean something. This is not decoration: gold reads as value earned, orange as caution, a hot Signal Orange as the one thing you should act on. The surfaces are flat and quiet, bordered by a soft khaki-gold hairline; depth comes from tonal layering, not drop shadows. Motion is Apple-fluid and single-purpose — controls dip toward the finger, overlays grow from the point they were summoned, and the one authored flourish is a recommendation's reasoning physically unfolding when you ask 'Why this?'.

The register is warm and editorial, never clinical and never loud. It should feel like a trusted adviser who shows their working: calm, exact, readable, and confident enough to leave most of the screen still. Anti-reference: the neon fintech dashboard, the black-box 'credit score' dial, the gamified confetti-and-streak app. Finance OS earns trust by being explicable, not exciting.
keyCharacteristics: Warm sunset-and-ink palette where every hue carries semantic meaning (gold = value, orange = caution, Signal Orange = action).
Flat, bordered surfaces; depth by tonal layering (bg → surface → surface-2), never by resting shadow.
Tabular, sans-serif numerals that lead every screen — money is the typography.
Reasoning is always one disclosure away; the product's POV is 'no black box'.
Restraint: generous quiet, the accent used sparingly, a single authored motion moment.
First-class light and dark, resolved with light-dark() and honoured before first paint.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange is action-only. It appears on the logo mark and the primary button, and it is never used to decorate, fill, or highlight. If a screen has Signal Orange in two places, one of them is wrong — its scarcity is exactly what makes 'do this' legible.

rules.name: The Hue-Means-Something Rule
rules.body: A warm colour is never decorative. Gold means value/gains, Kindled Orange means caution, Sunset Red means loss. A positive number rendered in orange, or a caution rendered in gold, is a bug — reach for the semantic token (text-pos / text-warn / text-neg), never a raw colour.

rules.name: The Sunlit-or-Midnight Rule
rules.body: Both schemes are first-class. Never hardcode a hex where a semantic token exists; every colour must survive the light-dark() flip, and the theme is applied before first paint (no flash).

rules.name: The AA-Orange Rule
rules.body: Every action and semantic colour clears WCAG AA (≥4.5:1) at body size: white on primary-strong, and primary-ink / pos / warn / neg / accent as text. Vivid #fc3d12 is kept only where 3:1 suffices — the logo mark and large / non-text fills. If a colour is used as normal-size text or behind white button text, it must be one of the AA-cleared tokens, never raw #fc3d12.

rules.name: The Tabular-Money Rule
rules.body: Every monetary figure uses tabular numerals (.tnum / font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) and never wraps. Money is set in the sans stack, not mono — the tabular figures do the alignment, the mono font is only for literal credentials.

rules.name: The Numbers-Lead Rule
rules.body: The biggest thing on any screen is a figure, not a heading. Section eyebrows are small, muted, and uppercase precisely so the value beneath them can be large and bare.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only to say 'this is floating above the page' (a popover, a drawer) or 'this is now stuck to the top' (the scrolled header) — never to add depth to a static card. If a resting card has a shadow, remove it.

dos: Do lead every screen with a large, bare, tabular figure and a small muted eyebrow above it.
Do reach for a semantic colour token by meaning — text-pos for gains, text-neg for loss, text-warn for caution — never a raw hex.

Do keep every action and semantic colour at ≥4.5:1 as text: bg-primary-strong for buttons, text-primary-ink for orange text/links; reserve vivid bg-primary (#fc3d12) for the logo mark and large / non-text fills.

Do guard a destructive, hard-to-reverse action (close account, delete goal, delete transaction) behind the two-step ConfirmButton — which also raises an Undo toast — so nothing fires on a single click and every confirmed action has a way back.
Do let the global :focus-visible ring show on every interactive element, and pad interactive text (links, disclosures) to a ≥24px touch target.

Do give every route a calm fallback — a shell-preserving loading skeleton, an error boundary with Try again (retry()), and a not-found — and turn an untrusted route param that can't resolve (a bad id) into a 404, not a 500.
Do keep surfaces flat; build structure from the border-border hairline and the bg→surface→surface-2 tonal ladder.
Do set money in the sans stack with tabular numerals (.tnum) and whitespace-nowrap.
Do make reasoning reachable — put the 'why' one disclosure away, and let it unfold.

Do explain finance jargon at its point of use — a dotted-underline Explainer term with a one-line plain-language gloss (or persistent helper text in a form), drawn from the single shared glossary so the wording stays consistent everywhere.
Do support both schemes through light-dark() tokens, and keep motion to transform/opacity so it degrades cleanly under reduced-motion.

Do give power users a keyboard path — the ⌘K command palette reaches every page and core action from one overlay, driven from the shared nav list so it never drifts, with the only accent its focus ring.

Do make a high-volume list triage-able — multi-select with a bulk bar (recategorise, rule, export, delete), "select all N matching" for cross-page reach applied by filter, a neutral surface-2 tint for ticked rows, and destructive bulk delete behind the same ConfirmButton + Undo as a single row.
donts: Don't use Signal Orange for anything but the brand mark and the primary action. No orange fills, dividers, or highlights.
Don't give a resting card a drop shadow — shadow means 'floating' or 'scroll-detached', nothing else.

Don't strip the :focus-visible ring (a bare outline-none with nothing in its place) — it's the keyboard user's only cue. A soft glow is still out; the focus indicator is a crisp 2px Signal-Orange line.
Don't set money or figures in the mono font — mono is only for literal credentials.
Don't show a black-box score or an unexplained number; if a figure can't be traced to accounts and transactions, it doesn't belong.
Don't let data tables reflow the page — scroll them horizontally inside their card.
